Read RFC 2545 in full, its short requirement and shell-materialized ledger, all 25 current tag entries and their enclosing bodies/helpers, and their width, scope and final-writer producers. Section 3 says: "The value of the Length of Next Hop Network Address field on a MP_REACH_NLRI attribute shall be set to 16, when only a global address is present, or 32 if a link-local address is also included in the Next Hop field." The four audit questions were judged afresh, without inheriting the earlier verdict. Q1: the literal MP_REACH length/address/NLRI assertions implement this exact sentence. Native IPv4 controls legal under SR Policy, mapped fields and capability-77 standalone fields are separate contracts, not claimed as global-plus-link-local proof. Q2: wrong length, missing valid delivery, omitted/extra pair address, illegal width admission or failure to apply a valid repair contradict the exact asserted output; recorded producer-break evidence was read only for its named break, with no new observation or freshness claim. Q3: genuine global and global/link-local controls retain their negotiated family, distinct recipient and valid complete NLRI; native-four, VPN-shaped, empty/eight-byte and invalid-second cases change the selected field after policy, with native withdrawals and unaffected legacy siblings checked independently. Q4: the corpus collectively pins both 16 and 32, on origination, final post-policy writes, both forwarding rails and stored replay. Per-unit evidence: TestSRPolicyConfigNextHopWire and TestSRPolicyEncodeNextHopWire compare the literal sixteen-byte IPv6 global, length byte, reserved byte, complete NLRI and Tunnel Encapsulation under both policy AFIs. TestFamilyNextHopOriginationAdmission (positive/negative tags) exercises API, queue drain and named commit, before/after replacement: valid globals require exactly one delivered MP_REACH with a sixteen-byte field; native four-byte substitutes under native IPv6 multicast/labeled fields require zero announcements, including actual socket bytes and commit accounting. TestFamilyNextHopForwardAdmission (both tags) runs cached and RS/export forwarding, requiring one exact native announcement or family withdrawal and one unchanged legacy sibling; 4/24/48-byte replacements are refused where forbidden, while global and later legal repairs survive. TestDefaultOriginateAppendsLinkLocalWhenSection3Holds and TestSendAnnounceAppendsLinkLocalWhenSection3Holds use a speaker-owned non-loopback global, a distinct on-link peer and one explicit connected prefix, and require socket MP_REACH bytes containing 0x20 plus both literal addresses. TestStaticGroupedResolvedNextHopWire checks literal 0x10 global fields for explicit and connected-session Self cases, both prefixes, exact announcement/EOR framing and successful ownership. TestSessionSendAnnounceAcceptsLinkLocalSecondAddress requires the literal pair and 0x20 at the socket; TestSessionSendAnnounceRefusesNonLinkLocalSecondAddress requires the specific encoding error and no bytes for a global second address. TestAPIBatchRefusesUnusableIPv6NextHop, TestQueuedOriginateRefusesUnusableIPv6NextHop and TestNamedCommitRefusesUnusableIPv6NextHop (two tags each) compare complete literal 0x10 global frames against zero announcement output for native IPv4 and unusable roles, retaining exact EOR, refusal and production accounting. TestOriginatedIPv6NextHopAdmissionAfterExportPolicy (two tags) applies the same oracle after raw export replacement on all three producers and checks an actual captured-owner queued writer with a surviving later IPv4 sibling. TestRFC2545EffectivePairPolicyAndMixedSibling (two tags) observes actual recipient socket output on cached and RS/export rails: selected 4/24/48, empty/eight-byte fields cannot announce; later valid 16/32 repairs supersede the obsolete raw field; pair scope controls preserve 32 on-link and trim to 16 off-link; independent legacy siblings remain. checkRFC2545NextHops requires the exact FRR global/link-local shape for the on-link prefix and sole global for a different off-link prefix on one session, plus the exact installed BGP/FIB link-local and surviving session. This complements the literal width assertions; it does not substitute receiver JSON for them. test/encode/new-v6.ci pins a complete 0x10 single-global frame. test/exabgp-compat/encoding/conf-llnh-update.ci pins a complete 0x20 pair frame with distinct configured owner and recipient. test/plugin/adj-rib-in-replay-rfc2545-next-hop.ci has separate live-control and requested-replay sequence expectations, both requiring the same full 0x20 pair frame on a real common link. Current production agrees: NextHopProfile.SelectAddress chooses representation once; NextHopOctets/NextHopLen count those selected address octets and WriteNextHops writes them, including only a profile's declared RD framing. MPReachNLRI.WriteTo writes that computed count and the same profile's address bytes; buildMPReachPlugin uses the selected profile width and writer. The direct writeAnnounceUpdate emits 16 or 32 from admitted optional link-local presence. ValidateFamilyNextHop/ValidateMPNextHop, Session.writeUpdateGated and egressNextHopWithheld reject inappropriate effective widths, while applyEgressNextHopScope preserves wrong-width input for admission and applies scope only to legal forms. No code, tests, tag claims or discrimination records were edited by this audit.
